title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access to a system, then used an AI agent to conduct the post-compromise attack automatically. The agent retrieved cloud credentials from the compromised system, used them to access AWS Secrets Manager for an SSH private key, and then connected to an internal database server. The entire chain from initial exploit to database access took less than one hour, with the agent adapting its commands in real time based on the output of each step.

The deployment failure was the use of an AI agent with autonomous access to sensitive systems and credentials. The agent was capable of executing commands, retrieving secrets, and moving laterally through infrastructure without human intervention or approval at each stage. It is not established whether the agent was intentionally deployed in this way or whether the attacker gained control of an agent designed for legitimate purposes.

A human review before credential retrieval and before database access, or restrictions preventing the agent from automatically using retrieved secrets for new connections, would have caught this attack before the database was reached.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team discovered an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent conducted post-compromise attacks in real time. An attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access, then harvested cloud credentials from the compromised system. The attacker used these credentials to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager and accessed an internal database server. The entire attack chain, from the initial compromise through database exfiltration, took less than one hour to complete. The attacker routed traffic through multiple Cloudflare Workers endpoints to disguise the source of the connection.

The research team identified four distinct signatures proving the attack was driven by an AI agent rather than a pre-written script. These included improvised database dumps targeting unknown systems, planning comments appearing during execution, commands structured for machine interpretation, and the attack chain using output from each step to inform the next. The attack demonstrates how AI-driven intrusions can adapt to unfamiliar environments in real time. The Sysdig team recommends immediately updating marimo software, auditing exposed systems for compromised credentials, and rotating all sensitive access keys and passwords as precautions.
